newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich expects Clinton to sign tax-cut bill.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich expects Clinton to sign tax-cut bill.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Thursday he would not expect President Clinton to veto tax cuts based solely on his objection to indexing capital gains tax rates for inflation.
"I find it extremely unlikely that if the last item (in dispute) were indexing, he will veto it over that," the Georgia Republican said at a news conference.
He spoke with House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer in opposition to the Clinton administration's effort to make the child tax credit refundable to those who pay no income tax.
The House tax bill would index capital gains tax rates to reduce the amount of tax investors would pay on gains due to inflation.
Gingrich and Archer compared the refundable child credit to a welfare increase. "In a tax-cut bill the focus ought to be on helping taxpayers," Gingrich said.
They urged Clinton to support an extension of the $500-per-child credit to children up to age 17. Clinton's proposal ended the tax credit at age 13.
"At the end of the day, I believe the president will sign the bill," Gingrich added.
The five-year $85 billion tax cut bill is to be brought to the full House for a vote next week. The Senate Finance Committee is voting on its version Thursday.
